terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. `node src/stock.ts` runs the stock count, and `npm run types` checks it with the settings in `tsconfig.json`.

tasks.title: Switch on noImplicitAny
tasks.description:
In `tsconfig.json`, switch `noImplicitAny` on. Then, under `// Task 1` in `src/stock.ts`, write the type of every parameter the compiler now asks for, and fix what it finds once they have types, so `tinsToOrder` gives how many tins it takes to bring a shelf up to the number given. Task 3 switches on the rest of `strict`.

Check reads your `tsconfig.json` the way the compiler does, and wants `noImplicitAny` on. It compiles your lines with your `tsconfig.json`, and with settings of its own that have `noImplicitAny` on: both must accept them. It refuses `any`, `as` and comments that start with `@ts-` in your lines. It compiles code of its own: passing a shelf and a number must compile, while text for the number, a blend for a shelf, or text for `shelfLine` must be refused. It calls both functions with shelves of its own.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's parts on `tsconfig.json` and on `noImplicitAny`.
Add `noImplicitAny` to `compilerOptions`, and run `npm run types`.
Write the type of each parameter it names.
Run `npm run types` again: once the parameters have types, it finds one more thing.
hints: A setting goes inside `compilerOptions`, as a name in double quotes, a colon and `true`, with a comma between it and the next one. `Unknown compiler option` means the name is spelt differently from the real one.
`Parameter 'shelf' implicitly has an 'any' type` asks you to say what `shelf` is. There is a type for a shelf at the top of the file. Once it is there, the compiler can check the body against it.
`"noImplicitAny": true` in `tsconfig.json`, then `tinsToOrder(shelf: Shelf, target: number)` and `shelfLine(shelf: Shelf)`, and `shelf.tins` where the body read a property a shelf does not have.

tasks.title: Switch on strictNullChecks
tasks.description:
In `tsconfig.json`, switch `strictNullChecks` on. Then, under `// Task 2` in `src/stock.ts`, fix what the compiler finds: `tinsOf` gives `0` for a blend that has no shelf, and `reorderNote` keeps giving `undefined` for a shelf that is not low, with a result type that says so.

Check reads your `tsconfig.json` the way the compiler does, and wants `strictNullChecks` on. It compiles your lines with your `tsconfig.json`, and with settings of its own that have `strictNullChecks` and `noImplicitAny` on: both must accept them. It refuses `any`, `as`, `!` after a value and comments that start with `@ts-` in your lines. It compiles code of its own that uses what `reorderNote` gives as text that is always there: that must be refused. It calls both functions with shelves of its own, and a blend without a shelf.
nextSteps: Add `strictNullChecks` to `compilerOptions`, and run `npm run types`.
In `tinsOf`, check the shelf before reading from it.
In `reorderNote`, say in the result type what the function really gives back.
hints: `'shelf' is possibly 'undefined'` means `find` may find nothing. The code reads `tins` from it anyway, and that is the error Node stopped with.
Check the value the way you learned in the issue on narrowing, and give back `0` in the branch where there is no shelf. For `reorderNote`, the result type can be a union.
`if (shelf === undefined) return 0` before `return shelf.tins`, and `): string | undefined {` on `reorderNote`.

tasks.title: Switch on all of strict
tasks.description:
In `tsconfig.json`, switch `strict` on, so every check it turns on is on. Then, under `// Task 3` in `src/stock.ts`, fix what the compiler finds, so that for text it cannot read, `countLine` still gives `'Could not read the count: '` and the message of the error `JSON.parse` throws.

Check reads your `tsconfig.json` the way the compiler does, and wants every check of `strict` on. It compiles your lines with your `tsconfig.json`, and with settings of its own that have `strict` on: both must accept them. It refuses `any`, `as` and comments that start with `@ts-` in your lines. It calls `countLine` with text of its own, some it can read and some it cannot.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's parts on what `strict` turns on and on a value that was thrown.
Set `strict` to `true` in `tsconfig.json`, and run `npm run types`.
Find out what `error` is before reading its message.
hints: `'error' is of type 'unknown'` comes from one of the checks `strict` turns on: anything can be thrown, not only an `Error`, so the compiler will not let you read `message` without looking first.
`instanceof Error` narrows a value to an `Error`, the way `typeof` narrowed to a number. For a thrown value that is not an Error, any text will do.
`"strict": true` in `tsconfig.json`, then `const reason = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)` and that `reason` in the line.

tasks.title: Switch on noUncheckedIndexedAccess
tasks.description:
In `tsconfig.json`, switch `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` on, beside `strict`. Then, under `// Task 4` in `src/stock.ts`, fix what the compiler finds: when no shelf is below its reorder point, `firstToReorder` gives `'Nothing to reorder'`.

Check reads your `tsconfig.json` the way the compiler does, and wants `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `strictNullChecks` on. It compiles your lines with your `tsconfig.json`, and with settings of its own that have `strict` and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` on: both must accept them. It refuses `any`, `as`, `!` after a value and comments that start with `@ts-` in your lines. It calls `firstToReorder` with shelves of its own, none of them low in some.
nextSteps: Add it to `compilerOptions`, and run `npm run types`.
Put the first item in a name of its own, and check it before reading its blend.
hints: `Object is possibly 'undefined'` points at `low[0]`: with this setting, an item read from a list may not be there, and here it is not when no shelf is low.
Checking `low.length` first does not help: the compiler does not connect the length with the item. Read the item into a `const`, and check that.
`const first = low[0]`, then `if (first === undefined) return 'Nothing to reorder'` and `return first.blend`.
